relationships.description: The environmental condition is one of the pinned settings that together make up a context variation's concrete execution environment, so the context variation is defined partly by the factors bound to it.
relationships.evidence: The coverage model file lists the factor (e.g. os: ubuntu-22.04) under the context variation's environment-factor bindings, or a CI matrix entry for that variation sets the factor's value.

relationships.description: The environmental condition is treated as a constituent dimension of an input partition, contributing an environment-dependent axis (such as locale) to the equivalence classes that divide that input field's domain.
relationships.evidence: The partition definition in the coverage model embeds the factor as one of its dimensions, or the partition's classes are keyed on the factor's value (e.g. locale-specific date formats).

relationships.description: The factor's pinned value is passed into the model-wide coverage summary so the report records the environment under which the totals were measured.
relationships.evidence: The generated coverage summary report contains an environment section listing the factor name and value captured from the test run's configuration.

relationships.description: The environmental condition points at a telemetry instrumentation setting, such as whether an auto-instrumentation plugin is enabled, because that setting changes how the tests behave or perform.
relationships.evidence: The factor's definition names the instrumentation config entry (e.g. OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_HTTP_ENABLED=false) that the test harness sets before SDK bootstrap.

relationships.description: The environmental condition identifies the deployment host, such as a specific VM size, container instance or cluster, whose characteristics the test run is pinned to.
relationships.evidence: The factor value matches a node declared in infrastructure code (e.g. a Terraform instance or Kubernetes cluster name) that the CI job targets as its test runner or deployment environment.

relationships.description: The environmental condition points at a specific equivalence class whose representative value it adopts, for example a locale factor pinned to the class used for a locale-sensitive input.
relationships.evidence: The factor's constraint in the coverage model cites the partition value's identifier as the source of its pinned value.

relationships.description: The environmental condition records which access-control policy is active in the test environment, because the policy in force changes which authorization outcomes tests observe.
relationships.evidence: The test environment configuration loads a named policy bundle (e.g. an OPA or XACML policy file) and the factor entry names that policy as its value.

relationships.description: The environmental condition pins the version or variant of a platform product, such as the operating system, language runtime or database engine, that the tests run against.
relationships.evidence: The CI matrix, Dockerfile base image or docker-compose service image tag (e.g. postgres:15.4, node:20) matches the system software and version named by the factor.

relationships.description: The environmental condition supplies one of the environment values a coverage requirement's combinatorial criterion must be exercised across, for example pairwise combination of OS and browser.
relationships.evidence: The coverage requirement's criterion definition lists the factor among the dimensions it combines, and the generated combination table includes the factor's values.

relationships.description: The environmental condition provides the concrete environment setting under which a test case sketch is designed to execute.
relationships.evidence: The test case sketch, or the parameterized test row or pytest marker that realizes it, specifies the factor's value as a precondition or fixture parameter.

relationships.description: The environmental condition is made available as a reusable environment definition within the coverage model that plans testing for the application.
relationships.evidence: The coverage model document declares the factor in its environment-factor catalogue, and context variations within that model refer to it by identifier.

notes: Composes into InputSpacePartition contradicts the factor's definition (environment, not SUT input); references PartitionValue is similarly suspect. Composes into ContextVariation should likely be aggregates, since factors are optionally bound and shareable. Flows-to CoverageSummary is odd: summaries total targets, requirements and sketches, not factors. Serves TestCoverageModel likely should be composed-by/aggregated-by.
